content.title: How many National Championships does UConn coach Geno Auriemma have?
content.text: Success is a capricious path where only the most outstanding people in their field enter, but on this path we find a very large list of characters who have earned a place in history. In women's college basketball, there is one person who has undoubtedly traveled this path and has been doing so for 40 years and countingThis is Geno Auriemma, the coach of the Connecticut University team, who is in his 40th season since arriving in 1985, and who has transformed the Huskies into a program of unparalleled excellence. For the experienced collegiate coach, in four decades he has achieved 1,217 career victories, setting the NCAA record. It is undoubtedly a fantastic feat, which has become an impressive number of championships.Such a tease! Paige Bueckers tries to piss off teammate Azzi Fudd ahead of the NCAA title gameGeno Auriemma's National Championships for the HuskiesSince 1985, Geno Auriemma has been the head coach of the University of Connecticut and it was not until 1995 that he won his first National Championship. However, his leadership skills have earned him 10 more collegiate titles to set a record 12 in total: (2000, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2009, 2010, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2025)In addition to including 12 NCAA championships, it has also recorded 24 Final Fours, six perfect seasons and 59 conference championships. There is no doubt that Geno Auriemma is one of the most outstanding coaches in women's college basketball and his legacy still resonates in the current NCAA season.Geno Auriemma in the Hall of FameIt was in 2006 when the NCAA authorities granted Geno Auriemma entry into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame and the Women's Basketball Hall of Fame. Among other achievements, Geno is the fourth women's basketball coach to reach 1,000 victories in his career and was the one who reached the mark in the shortest time, in his 1,135th game and has the best winning percentage in the sport (.882).Under Auriemma's leadership, 27 Huskies have been selected as WBCA All-Americans with 48 total honors, while a Husky has been named National Player of the Year 14 times. He is the first coach in women's basketball history to guide a team to five consecutive Final Four appearances on two separate occasions and set a record with 14 consecutive Final Fours between 2008 and 2022.
